title: Byte Streams: FileInputStream and FileOutputStream
learningObjectives: Read raw file data using FileInputStream and byte arrays
Write binary data using FileOutputStream and byte buffers
Detect end-of-stream using the documented negative-one result
Copy files while writing only the number of bytes actually read
Close input and output streams safely after every operation

understand.concept: FileInputStream reads bytes and FileOutputStream writes bytes. The read method returns -1 at end of stream. For larger files, use a byte buffer.
understand.whyItMatters: Byte streams preserve raw bytes and are appropriate for binary data such as images, archives and arbitrary file copies. Correct buffering and end-of-stream handling prevent truncated output and unnecessary one-byte I/O operations.
understand.analogy: A byte stream is like moving sealed numbered packets: the program copies each byte without interpreting it as a letter or character.
understand.analogyLimit: Bytes do not inherently represent text. Decoding arbitrary bytes as characters without knowing the encoding can corrupt or misinterpret data.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var in = new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[]{65,66,67})) { System.out.println((char)in.read()); } } }
examples.explanation: Reads the first byte and interprets its ASCII value as a character for demonstration.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var out = new java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream()) { out.write(new byte[]{65,66}); System.out.println(out.size()); } } }
examples.explanation: Writes two bytes to an output stream.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var in = new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[]{65,66,67})) { int b; while((b=in.read())!=-1) System.out.print((char)b); } } }

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var in = new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[]{1,2,3,4})) { byte[] buffer = new byte[2]; int count=in.read(buffer); System.out.println(count + ":" + buffer[1]); } } }
examples.explanation: Reads a block of bytes into a buffer.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println(new java.io.ByteArrayInputStream(new byte[0]).read()); } }
examples.explanation: Confirms that an empty stream immediately reports end-of-stream.

practise.guidedTask: Copy a temporary binary file with FileInputStream and FileOutputStream using a fixed-size byte buffer. Compare source and destination bytes.
practise.independentTask: Implement a byte-copy method that loops until read returns -1, writes only the bytes actually read and closes both streams safely.
hints: Choose the API that matches the data representation and operation.
Test empty, normal and failure cases; verify exact output or file contents.
practise.challenge: Test an empty file, a file smaller than the buffer, a file larger than the buffer and binary bytes containing zero values.
